sentences.text: Cerasinops hodgskissi is the only known species in the extinct genus Cerasinops, representing a small ceratopsian dinosaur.
This animal possessed a wide, thick skull equipped with a parrot-like beak that ended in a strong rim.

Estimates for its size vary significantly; one assessment suggests a total length of 2.5 meters and a mass of 175 kilograms, while another places the length at approximately 1.70 meters and the weight between 13 and 18 kilograms.
Fossils of this dinosaur have been found in the lower Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dated between 77 and 80.2 million years ago.
The species was originally discovered by Jack Horner in 1983, but it was not named and described until 2007 by Brenda Chinnery and Jack Horner.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as MOR 300, preserves about 80% of the skull and skeleton, including most limbs but excluding the hands and tail.
Cerasinops possessed an extra tooth at the front of the jaw and utilized a unique chewing method distinct from other Asian and North American ceratopsians.
Paleontologists debate whether Cerasinops is a basal ceratopsian or a sister taxon to the family Leptoceratopsidae, though its exact placement within the group remains variable.
Despite this uncertainty, the genus is generally classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae, which serves as its parent group.
Cerasinops lived during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 80 million years ago, in what is now North America.
